trigger: "archival solution based on Amazon S3 Glacier to enforce regulatory and compliance controls"
answer: S3 Glacier vault with a Vault Lock policy (WORM controls, locked from future edits)
trap: The S3 Access Control List option fails because ACLs manage access only and cannot enforce compliance; the lifecycle policy option fails because lifecycle rules transition or expire objects but cannot enforce compliance.
memory_hook: Compliance locks = Vault Lock, not ACLs or lifecycles

trigger: "all changes to the items stored in the DynamoDB tables must be logged in near real-time"
answer: DynamoDB Streams → Lambda → Kinesis Data Streams → Kinesis Data Analytics → SNS
trap: The CloudTrail option captures API calls, not item-level changes; and the direct Lambda-to-KDA option fails because KDA only accepts KDS or Firehose sources.
memory_hook: item changes = Streams, KDA needs KDS

trigger: "many files are processed twice" while adding instances; raw uploads sit on shared EFS scanned by polling
answer: Upload to S3, S3 event triggers Lambda that enqueues to SQS, workers read SQS and scale on queue depth per instance
trap: The API Gateway option fails because its 10 MB payload limit cannot carry 1 GB uploads; the EventBridge-to-Lambda option is a roundabout route to the same queue.
memory_hook: 1 GB upload → direct S3, not API Gateway

trigger: "both stateful and stateless client-server communications" via API Gateway APIs
answer: Amazon API Gateway REST APIs for stateless client-server communication and WebSocket APIs for stateful, full-duplex communication (option C)
trap: Option D makes REST stateful, but REST APIs are HTTP-based and stateless; option B reverses the pairing by making WebSocket stateless, which ignores its persistent full-duplex connection.

trigger: "429 Too Many Requests" at peak with Lambda never invoked, plus "separate quota" for premium customers
answer: API Gateway account-level throttle, fixed with API keys as client identifiers in usage plans for per-client limits
trap: Option C blames a per-method limit, but 429s hit multiple methods, so the limit is account-level; Option A's Lambda-level throttling in usage plans isn't a real feature.
memory_hook: Lambda not invoked = API Gateway throttled; premium quota = usage plan + API key

trigger: "only the most frequently accessed results are available as cached data locally while backing up all results on Amazon S3"
answer: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached volume mode: hot data local, full volume in S3
trap: The Stored Volume option keeps the entire data set on-premises; that fails because only frequently accessed results should be cached locally.
memory_hook: Cached = hot local, full copy in S3

trigger: "140 TB" archive due in S3 by Monday over a "10-Gbps Direct Connect connection" with a private VIF in place
answer: Public virtual interface on the existing Direct Connect connection, then copy to S3 over it
trap: Option B's private VIF reaches only VPC private IPs, not S3. Option C (Snowball Edge) takes about a week end to end, missing the deadline.
memory_hook: S3 is public = public VIF; Snowball is for weeks, DX is for days

trigger: "without moving away from the underlying relational database schema" plus "work on a global scale"
answer: Amazon Aurora Global Database: one relational MySQL-compatible database spanning regions with fast local reads
trap: DynamoDB Global Tables gives multi-region read and write, but it is NoSQL and breaks the existing relational schema requirement.

trigger: "improve the reliability and availability" for disaster recovery, restore "within five hours", "most cost-effective way"
answer: Automated cross-region snapshot copy for Redshift, then restore the cluster in the other Region from that Region's snapshot, with a CloudFormation StackSet to launch it
trap: Option A and option B both keep a second live Redshift cluster running, which is not cost-effective; option D's Auto Scaling groups for Redshift nodes is not a Redshift feature.
memory_hook: Cheap Redshift DR = copy snapshots cross-region, not a second live cluster

trigger: S3TA "did not result in an accelerated transfer" with uploads from the internet
answer: No transfer charges: S3 bills no data transfer-in, and S3 Transfer Acceleration bills only for accelerated transfers
trap: The S3TA-charges option fails because nothing was accelerated, and the both-charges option fails because uploads into S3 from the internet carry no S3 transfer fee.
memory_hook: Uploads in are free; S3TA bills only accelerated bytes

trigger: "shared and centrally-managed VPCs" for business units needing high interconnectivity within one organization
answer: VPC sharing via Resource Access Manager: share one or more subnets with accounts in the same AWS Organization
trap: The VPC peering option sharing subnets fails because peering links two VPCs and cannot share subnets or centrally manage a VPC; sharing the whole VPC fails because only subnets can be shared.
memory_hook: Share subnets, not VPCs; peering is not central

trigger: "huge delays in uploading large video files" from overseas facilities to an S3 bucket
answer: S3 Transfer Acceleration plus S3 multipart uploads: edge routing over CloudFront for distance, parallel parts for large objects
trap: Direct Connect takes months to provision and is overkill; the Site-to-Site VPN option runs over the same internet path and gives no upload speedup; Global Accelerator targets application endpoints, not S3 uploads.
memory_hook: Long distance = Transfer Acceleration; big files = multipart

trigger: 200 TB to S3 "in the shortest possible time" over Direct Connect and VPN bandwidth
answer: AWS Snowball Edge appliances: split the data across three devices (about 80 TB each) and ship them to AWS for import into S3
trap: The 500 Mbps Direct Connect and 1 Gbps VPN options look fast but need roughly 40 and 20 days for 200 TB, while Snowball ships in 5-7 days.
memory_hook: Huge data + tight deadline = ship the disks

trigger: "I/O intensive" workload "constrained on the IOPS" needing +3,000 IOPS per instance, "MOST cost-efficient"
answer: Resize the EBS gp2 volume from 3 TB to 4 TB: gp2 baseline is 3 IOPS per GiB, so +1,000 GiB adds 3,000 IOPS
trap: Option C, io1 at 12,000 IOPS, works but costs more per GB-month; option B (EFS) costs about 3x gp2 per GB, and option A (S3) cannot serve frequent random updates
memory_hook: gp2 = 3 IOPS per GiB, so add GiB to add IOPS

trigger: "disaster recovery strategy for all the Amazon RDS databases" with options on snapshot sharing, RTO, and Read Replica failover
answer: Manual DB snapshots copied and shared across Regions and accounts; RTO as hours to restore; Read Replicas and backups cross-Region
trap: Read Replica failover is manual, unlike Multi-AZ; automated snapshots cannot be shared, only manual snapshots (up to 20 accounts); RPO, not RTO, measures data loss.
memory_hook: RTO = hours back up; RPO = data lost
